chunks: Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام said: The Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله led his companions in salat while seated, and when he finished, he said:
"None of you should lead others in salat while seated after me."

key_terms.بَعْدِي: after me; indicating that this allowance was not for others after the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.بِأَصْحَابِهِ: with his companions; indicating a congregational setting
key_terms.جَالِسًا: while seated; the central legal condition discussed in the hadith
key_terms.رَسُولَ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, whose action and statement establish the ruling here
key_terms.صَلَّى: performed salat; here it refers to leading the congregational prayer
key_terms.يَؤُمَّنَّ: should lead as Imam in prayer

ai.seo_question: Can a person lead congregational salat while seated?
ai.summary: Imam Abu Jaʿfar عليه السلام relates that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله once led the companions in salat while seated, then prohibited others from doing so after him. The hadith indicates a specific legal distinction for the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله and addresses the ruling of leading congregational salat while seated.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1118 - Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said:
"The Messenger of Allah (sw) once led his companions in prayer while seated. When he finished, He (sw) said:
'None of you should lead others in prayer while seated after me.'".
